coverage.assessment: The clerk's Milan-to-Dresden map check loses its Lombardy motive. 'Luckily for him' loses the women's moral sense that answers the preceding dilemma. Beethoven, Berlin nightmare and Thuringen setups survive in 007's revision.

Stelvio geography thins: the Valtellina and the Jäger officers' answering courtesy are cut, so the barricade passage is less grounded. Other pronouns and entrances, including 'joined them' for the Kuhns, remain clear.
The only performed lines, '"Sir, I am a tourist!"' and the Gibbon quotation, are intact and correctly framed. No attribution problems.

The moral dilemma loses 'Not that Adams felt any real doubt' and 'it might happen that the good were robbed'. 'Two great experiments... third' stays speculative. The Garibaldi Autobiography conditional is cut whole, which is allowed. Seward support is not anticipated.
The old man's retrospective shame over the Courier letters and the young man's unawareness ('posing for a Gibbon') are cut, flattening the young/old distinction. Nothing is disclosed prematurely.
The ledger voice and aphorisms survive. Small asides ('half-a-dozen such' impressions, 'Berlin jurist', the Jäger/Cacciatori parallel) are cut, mostly as defensible compression.
Rome-as-vice loses its causal premise. The 'disunited' Germany of the essentials is gone. The Browning anecdote no longer shows how Rome dwarfs teachers before 'Perhaps it meant nothing.'
Ara Coeli, Mrs. Kuhn and Palermo endpoints are intact on both sides. The King plant was cut under its optional authorization, and 022 introduces King coherently without it.

strengths: All eight verbatim units survive in context, including the escalating 'Why! Why!! Why!!!' beside the blind beggar and the glow-worm deflation.
The Stelvio barricade sentence ('the flash of the gun barrels was lost in the flash of the snow') and Mrs. Kuhn's gasp are kept whole.
The Garibaldi sphinx paragraph keeps its full chain of conditional identities (Napoleon, Spartacus, Condottiere) and 'The student was none the wiser.'

The accidental-education ledger runs cleanly from the Beethoven comparison, through 'There were no accidents in Dresden', to 'mixed emotions but no education', supported by 007's surviving Beethoven scene.
summary: The revision keeps every verbatim item and the planned scenes: Thuringen, the Stelvio, the Dresden tally, Rome, Ara Coeli, Browning, Palermo and Paris. All dependencies survive except the authorized King cut. The revision's new trims, beyond the first draft, remove several hinges that make Adams's arguments work: why the clerk measures from Milan, the 'good were robbed' turn of the moral dilemma, the women's-moral-sense link behind 'Luckily for him', Germany's disunity, and the 'everything had a cause' premise for Rome. It also cuts two marks of retrospective distance and weakens the Browning/'Rome dwarfs teachers' logic. None of these is a blocker. Each can be repaired by restoring a sentence that the first draft already had.
